log.msg: ITEM 1 VERDICT - absorb is a documented NO. Measured: it drops dead space 80-93% -> 8-68%, but it does it by breaking the width words - the Finder small rail went 252px -> 1152px with label and chevron 900px apart, and the deepest prose column stretched one sentence to 1152px (past the 40em measure the words exist to hold). It also never closes the void: still 64-68% dead at 3440/3840. Shipped instead: the leftover row PAINTS as empty column slots (a repeating --line hairline every 14em on .page-columns-row + an opaque body floor).

ITEM 2 root cause - the hover rule was NOT missing: .page-column-item:hover set background: var(--tint). In lew42 --tint (#f8f8f8) is LIGHTER than --wash (#f2f2f2), which is what a column body sits on - the row lit up by six points of lightness in the wrong direction. Replaced with a translucent color-mix of --ink (6% hover / 12% press), which darkens whatever it is over, so it also works on the --tint and --surface recipe columns.

CORE BUG (coordinator item) fixed at the cause. The contract now asks the question its own record says it means - an ancestor is REPLACED BY A SIBLING, not by "the leaf is not inside me". Verified by selector diff on 6 routes: the ONLY page in the whole set classified differently is the generator page--list (old rule hid it, new rule shows it). Doc root, doc/css, homepage, uses/split and finder-deep are byte-identical. generator.css line 36 is now DEAD - left in place (their fence), safe to delete.

NAME COLLISION, caught by the probe: the new core method was first called opens(), and overview/columns/uses/inbox/page.js already carries a page field opens: 0 (messages activated). The field shadowed the method and the whole page died on "this.opens is not a function" - a core method named after a plain noun squats page state. Renamed default_column(), matching the *_column family.

census: 31 of 34 routes byte-identical before/after; the 3 that changed are exactly the collapsed recipes now opening a column. Only console error site-wide is a pre-existing 404 on /framework/web/ (present in the BEFORE run too, not mine).

assign.outcome:
**The column system's empty screen, fixed — and `absorb` measured and rejected with the pictures to show why.**

**1 · The void (recon #2/#3).** A columns host that has opened one column left **80% of the row grey at 1280 and 93% at 3840**. *Absorb was implemented and measured, and it is a documented no:* it closes the numbers (→8–68%) by breaking the words — the Finder's `small` rail grew 252px → **1152px** with the chevrons 900px from their labels, and the deepest prose column stretched one sentence to 1152px, past the 40em measure the words exist to hold. It also never closed the void (still 68% at 3840). **Shipped instead: the leftover is drawn as the column slots it is** — one repeating `--line` hairline per `small` track, plus an opaque body floor. Nothing moves, nothing is measured, no DOM.

![before — 93% grey](void-before-3840.png)
![after — the row reads as a column browser](void-after-3840.png)
![the absorb that was rejected](absorb-rejected-3440.png)

**2 · Hover was not missing — it was pointing the wrong way.** `.page-column-item:hover` set `background: var(--tint)`, and in lew42 `--tint` (#f8f8f8) is **lighter** than the `--wash` (#f2f2f2) a column body sits on. Now a translucent `color-mix` of `--ink` (6% hover / 12% press), which darkens whatever it is over — so it also works on the `--tint`/`--surface` recipe columns. The `×` gained a 24px target, a fill and `--prim-ink`. ![](hover-row.png)

**3 · Columns in a panel, both seams.** `.pages`' `.default` rule is split: the sheet half says `:not(.columns)`, and a host asks the region for a flex share only — measured in isolation, a host that was capped at **640px + 48px padding** now takes its full 1400px. And `render_column()` reads `classes` (additive — a column has no shape to choose).

**4 · The arrangement contract, root-caused** (the coordinator's item). The test asked *"is the leaf inside me"*; its own record says it means *"was I replaced by a sibling"*. Those are complements only until a leaf lands in a **cousin** region — the generator's `tabs > list > leaf`, hidden at 0px with no error. Now `.active-ancestor:not(:has(~ .page:is(.active-page, .active-ancestor)))`, same (0,4,0). **Verified by selector diff across the homepage, the Doc root, `doc/css`, `uses/split` and a five-deep Finder: exactly one element in the whole set is classified differently — the generator's own page.** A 34-route visible-page census was byte-identical on 31 routes; the 3 that moved are the recipes below.

**5 · Collapsed recipes.** The cause was that no seam existed to say it. A child now takes `classes: "default"` and `Page.default_column()` builds it — the host arrives with one column open, and Page.css stands it down the moment a real one is routed. Three labs fixed, one word each: dead space 80–93% → 0–61%, no width word touched. ![](recipe-open-after-3440.png)

**6 · Pickups.** `flush-wall` moved to the core `bleed` word and `.page-grids-flush` is **deleted** (its pre-committed deletion fired); the `padding` lab's "Flush" recipe is now actually flush, so its verdict line stopped lying; `readme.md` gained a line each for roles and panels; `doc/columns.md` + `doc/roles.md` link the four `uses/` exemplars.

**Docs:** [`doc/columns.md`](/framework/core/Page/doc/columns/) — the absorb verdict, the `default` column, the empty slots · [`doc/css.md`](/framework/core/Page/doc/css/) — the contract fix · [`readme.md`](/framework/core/Page/).

**Left, deliberately:** `generator.css`'s `(0,5,0)` stopgap is now **dead** but stays (their fence) — safe to delete; `uses/split` can drop `activated(){ this.view.ac("default") }` for `classes: "default"`, make its browse panel a plain `pages` region, and retire `uses.css`'s `.page-uses-stage > .page` flex rule — all logged, none touched; `core/Page/page.js` `methods:` wants `default_column` (their fence). `/framework/web/` 404s — pre-existing, present in the before run. Not attempted: the recon's generator-side items (#1, #6, #7, #12) and the `rolls` wall (#5), which are the sibling's fence.
